propositions: transport.py has grown to 799 LOC (at file cap) due to reactive splits that did not establish natural homes for new operations, forcing repeated rescue trims
previous extractions (retry.py, transitions.py) were mechanical relocations under cap pressure that re-exported names as a facade, leaving no obvious destination for new capabilities
the class already implements four capability Protocols defined in _backend.py (TicketTransport, SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, SupportsAbsenceProbe) that form natural module boundaries

relocation splits transport.py into five capability-aligned mixins (_base, _issues, _hierarchy, _links, _people) all within the 100–500 LOC target, composed by a thin transport.py root that preserves the single class and Protocol conformance
the relocation moves only text via mixin composition (preserving cache, _call_logged wrapper, and Protocol conformance) without editing test assertions or changing behavior
package docstring documents the organizing principle (one module per capability Protocol) so future operations have a determined home by capability rather than by available headroom
